ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION
DIRECTIVE FOR PRESCHOOL EDUCATION
CENTER

ARTICLE 1. PURPOSE:
The purpose of the GTU Preschool Education Center is to:
1- Assist the academic and administrative staff of GTU by providing an environment that fosters the
development of children aged 3-6 years in terms of physical, mental, social, and emotional aspects,
and enhances their creativity in accordance with the requirements of educational science, thus
supporting parents by ensuring a safer working environment improving their work efficiency
2- Prepare children for primary school, develop their Turkish language skills, and foster problem-
solving, thinking, and decision-making skills
3- Establish, support, and sustain communication between the school and the family to ensure
continuity in education
4- Guide families on educational matters through training programs
ARTICLE 2. BASIC PRINCIPLES OF THE CENTER:
1- No discrimination is allowed based on race, language, religion, gender, sect, political belief, or social
origin regarding the child and their family.
2- Every child is unique and cannot be subject to different practices due to their family.
3- The Preschool Education Center operates in accordance with Atatürk’s Principles and Reforms, and
the requirements of the modern world.
ARTICLE 3. DEFINITIONS:
Terms mentioned in this directive refer to the following:
Rectorate/University/GTU: Gebze Technical University Rectorate
Rector: Rector of Gebze Technical University
Directorate: GTU Directorate of Health, Culture and Sports
GTU Preschool Education Center/Center/Kindergarten: The center where children of GTU staff are cared
for and educated according to the purposes stated in Article 1
Parent: Mother and father of children attending the center
Guardian: GTU staff member assigned custody of a child whose family’s unity has been disrupted
ARTICLE 4. GROUPS AND THE ASSIGNED PERSONNEL:
Groups are formed in the Preschool Education Center considering the children’s age, physical conditions,
and psychological and social development levels, as well as the building’s physical conditions. The number
of children and personnel per group is determined accordingly.
The following principles are considered when forming groups:

A group consists of up to 15 children aged 3-6 years (36-72 months). Each group is assigned at least one
educator (teacher) and, where possible, additional support staff.
ARTICLE 5. PERSONNEL, COMMITTEES, AND THEIR DUTIES, AUTHORITIES, AND
RESPONSIBILITIES:
The personnel structure of the Gebze Technical University Preschool Education Center is as follows:
1- Principal
2- Administrative Officer
3- Child Development and Education Specialist
4- Social Service Specialist
5- Child Psychologist
6- Educator (Teacher)
7- Pediatrician
8- Nurse
9- Nutritionist
10- Education Assistant (Caregiver)
11- Cook
12- Support Staff (Attendant-Guard)
13- Executive Committee
14- Expenditures Audit Committee
The required personnel from the above list are employed based on the capacity of the Preschool Education
Center and the resources of GTU.
A. PRINCIPAL:
The individual appointed as the Principal must have a minimum a four-year degree in Child Development and
Education, Preschool Education, or Child Health and Education. If no such person is available, a Social Service
Specialist, Psychologist, or a GTU staff member deemed appropriate by the Rector may be assigned.
The Principal’s responsibilities include:
1- Ensuring the center operates in line with its purpose and the provisions of this directive
2- Organizing and supervising the division of labor among staff to ensure the best services for the children
3- Managing official correspondence and administrative duties among the kindergarten, the Directorate, and
the Rectorate
4- Identifying and communicating the needs for the continuation of care and education to the Directorate of
Health, Culture and Sports
The Principal reports to the Director of the Health, Culture and Sports for fulfilling these duties and exercising
these authorities.
If necessary, the Rector may assign an Assistant Principal to assist the Principal in performing these duties.
B. ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER:
The Administrative Officer’s responsibilities include:

1- Maintaining proper keeping of records and correspondence. Handling secretarial and accounting tasks for
the kindergarten;
2- Managing inventory and overseeing related counting, inventory, and recording tasks;
3- Performing other tasks assigned by the Principal related to the scope of their duties.
The Administrative Officer reports to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center.
C. CHILD DEVELOPMENT AND EDUCATION SPECIALIST:
The Child Development and Education Specialist must have a minimum four-year degree in Child Development
and Education or Child Health and Education.
The responsibilities include:
1- Preparing educational programs aligned with the children’s physical, emotional, linguistic, and social
development
2- Assisting in preparing the environment and procuring tools and materials ne eded for program
implementation
3- Supervising the implementation of the prepared programs and directly implementing them if t here are
insufficient educators
4- Monitoring children’s development and education, and collaborating with relevant professionals for
children with atypical development
5- Conducting studies and research aligned with the purpose of the center, within available resources
6- Coordinating among the education staff (teachers)
7- Organizing and participating in in-service training programs
8- Acting as a deputy in the absence of the Principal
The Child Development and Education Specialist reports to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center.
D. SOCIAL SERVICE SPECIALIST:
The Social Service Specialist must be a graduate of the Social Services Academy or the Social Work Department
of Hacettepe University.
Responsibilities include:
1. Conducting initial interviews with families applying to the kindergarten and preparing social investigation
reports, as well as assisting with admission procedures
2. Carrying out the necessary work to resolve children’s adaptation issues and ensuring their integration into
the kindergarten
3. Establishing harmony among the family, the child, and the kindergarten, and offering su ggestions to
families as needed
4. Organizing and participating in in-service training programs
5. Coordinating the use of university ’s and external resources to enhance kindergarten services, and
organizing and supervising volunteer contributions when necessary
6. Contributing to studies and research aligned with the center’s purpose, within available resources
7. Ensuring regular keeping of records related to their duties
The Social Service Specialist reports to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center.

E. CHILD PSYCHOLOGIST:
The Child Psychologist must hold a four-year degree in Psychology.
Responsibilities include:
1. Assessing children’s intelligence, abilities, mental state, and psychosocial development during enrollment and
leaving processes using various methods, and contributing to professional practices aimed at fostering a healthy
personality in children
2. Contributing to studies and research aligned with the center’s purpose, within available resources
3. Organizing and participating in in-service training programs
4. Keeping records required by their duties and related to their activities
The Child Psychologist reports to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center.
F. EDUCATOR (TEACHER):
Educators must be graduates of Preschool Education programs or, at a minimum, the Child Development and
Education Department of a Girls’ Vocational High School.
Responsibilities include:
1. Implementing the prepared educational programs in the classroom and preparing and organizing necessary tools
and materials
2. Being responsible for the tools, equipment, and furniture assigned to their group
3. Assisting new children in adapting to the classroom and school environment
4. Guiding caregivers (nannies) in helping children develop basic habits
5. Participating in in -service training programs and contributing to their planning an d implementation when
necessary
Educators report to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center.
G. PEDIATRICIAN:
A Pediatric Specialist is required at the Preschool Education Center. If unavailable, a pediatrician from GTU's
Medico-Social Center will be benefited from under an appropriate program approved by the Directorate of Health,
Culture and Sports. If both are unavailable, the GTU Institutional Doctor will take on this responsibility.
Responsibilities include:
1- Conducting initial health examinations for children upon enrollment and keeping health records
2- Performing routine health checks, ensuring vaccinations are administered, and overseeing other necessary
health-related tasks
3- Monitoring and ensuring the health and hygiene conditions of the center
4- Collaborating with the Principal to take necessary precautions against epidemics and infectious diseases
5- Participating in organizing and implementing in-service training programs
6- Providing necessary health information to children, educators, and other personnel
7- Informing parents about health where necessary
The Pediatrician reports to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center for the execution of these duties.

H. NURSE:
The responsibilities include:
1- Ensuring that the Preschool Education Center meets hygiene standards
2- Assisting the pediatrician in all health-related tasks
3- Participating in the organization and implementation of in-service training programs where necessary
I. NUTRITIONIST:
The Nutritionist must hold a minimum four-year degree in Nutrition from a recognized institution.
The responsibilities include:
1- Designing nutrition programs tailored to the children's age and health conditions, taking into account their daily
calorie requirements
2- Ensuring that nutrition programs are conducted in a regular and hygienic manner
3- Identifying necessary tools and materials related to nutrition and reporting them to the Principal
4- Carrying out other tasks as assigned by the Principal related to nutrition
J. EDUCATION ASSISTANT (CAREGIVER):
The responsibilities include:
1- Assisting children with activities such as play, rest, meals, cleanliness, and educational tasks under the
supervision of the teacher
2- Preparing snacks, arranging tables, and assisting children during meals
3- Helping children with hygiene after using the restroom
4- Assisting children during nap time, undressing, dressing, and ensuring the proper supervision of children during
rest periods
5- Maintaining the order and safety of the children’s play and sleeping areas and ensuring the protection of their
belongings
6- Keeping laundry, bedding, and all necessary materials ready for use at all times
7- Performing other tasks as assigned by the Principal
The Educational Assistant (Caregiver) reports to the Principal of the Preschool Education Center.
K. COOK:
A cook is assigned to prepare meals for children in the Preschool Education Center. If unavailable, this
responsibility can be delegated to a trained staff member.
The responsibilities include:
1- Preparing meals according to the daily meal plan, under the supervision and guidance of the Nutritionist,
ensuring health standards and maintaining food quality and presentation
2- Using foodstuffs economically and appropriately
3- Keeping kitchen tools and equipment clean, maintaining the overall cleanliness of the kitchen
L. SUPPORT STAFF (ATTENDANT/GUARD):
The Support Staff member is required to perform the duties assigned by the Principal of the Preschool Education
Center.
M. EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE:

The Executive Committee consists of the Vice-Rector overseeing the Directorate of Health, Culture, and Sports as
the Chair, along with the Director and/or Branch Manager of the Directorate of Health, Culture, and Sports, and
the Preschool Principal.
The responsibilities include:
1- Undertaking activities to develop the services provided by the Preschool Education Center and evaluating the
outcomes at the end of the year
2- Determining the preschool fees in accordance with the related year’s Budget Implementation Instructions
3- Determining the total capacity of the center and evaluating applications for enrollment based on the admission
criteria to select children accordingly
4- Identifying and ensuring the procurement of all necessary resources for the center
N. EXPENDITURES AUDIT COMMITTEE:
To audit expenditures, the Rector may establish a three -member committee consisting of one academic staff
member, one administrative staff member, and one parent. The committee submits its findings in a report to the
Rectorate after completing its inspection.
ARTICLE 6. DETERMINATION OF QUOTA, ENROLLMENT, AND ADMISSION CRITERIA:
The criteria to be considered for enrollment are as follows:
1- At least one parent must be a staff member at GTU.
2- The child must be at least 3 years old (36 months) and must be toilet-trained.
3- Evaluation will be made based on priority order.
When enrolling a child in the preschool, the priority order is as follows:
a) Children of the staff working at the GTU Preschool Education Center and children who are already enrolled.
b) Both parents work at GTU.
c) The mother works at GTU, and the father works elsewhere.
d) The father works at GTU, and the mother works elsewhere.
e) The father works at GTU, and the mother does not work.
f) For those with equal conditions, the length of service at GTU is taken into consideration, with staff who have
served longer being given priority.
The staff member submitting the application is considered the guardian.
Determination of Quota:
Letters of application are accepted between June and August every year. If vacancies in quota arise during the year,
applications that meet the criteria will be evaluated in order of priority.
The quotas are determined by the Executive Committee of the GTU Preschool Education Center, based on the
physical conditions of the building and available staff.
Quota distribution is as follows:
a) 40% of total quota is allocated to children of academic staff.
b) 40% is allocated to children of administrative staff.
c) 20% is reserved for children from the Rectorate’s quota.
The right to admission and the priority order for the Preschool Education Center cannot be transferred or altered
in any way.

Children with infectious or severe diseases, severe psychological disorders, or those with underdeveloped
intelligence and physical development may be admitted to a special section of the preschool if such a section is
opened.
Children who exhibit these types of issues during their development process, even if they are enrolled in the
preschool, may have their enrollment canceled by the Preschool Education Center Principal with the decision of
the Executive Committee, and be transferred to special education institutions.
ARTICLE 7. WORKING HOURS, ATTENDANCE, AND FEES:
1- Opening Hours and Work Schedule:
a) The opening and closing hours, as well as the working hours and rest periods, are determined by the Executive
Committee, taking into account seasonal conditions, the surrounding environment, and the specific characteristics
of the institution.
b) Unless otherwise decided, the working hours are from 08:30 AM to 05:15 PM, in alignment with GTU service
bus hours.
c) The center will be closed on weekends and public holidays.
d) In cases such as infectious diseases or severe weather conditions that may adversely affect the children, the
Executive Committee may decide, with the Rector’s approval, to close the center. No fee refunds will be issued
for such closures.
e) Unless otherwise decided by the Executive Committee, the center will be closed for one month from 1st to 31st
August and one week in February every year.
f) The responsibility of the staff regarding the children is only during the hours when the center is open.
2- Attendance Conditions:
a) Children must be brought to the preschool by 09:30 AM, except for significant reasons.
b) If a child is absent for more than a week due to health reasons, the absence must be certified with a doctor’s
report.
c) Children with contagious diseases will not be accepted to the preschool. They will be readmitted once a doctor
certifies that they have recovered.
d) Except in emergency cases (such as accidents, death, the parent’s temporary leave from the university, or the
child’s difficulty in adapting to the school at the beginning of the year), enrollment suspension is not allowed.
Fees:
a) Fees are to be paid in advance.
b) School fees must be paid as long as the child’s enrollment remains active.
c) If the child’s enrollment is canceled, no fee refund will be provided.
d) If the Preschool Education Center is closed for its annual August holiday, no fee will be charged for that month.
ARTICLE 8. TERMINATION OF ENROLLMENT:
The child’s enrollment with the Preschool Education Center may be terminated in the following cases:
1- If it is found that there is an error in the documents submitted for the child’s admission,
2- If the conditions for admission change,
3- If the child is absent for one month without valid excuses,
4- If the child is absent for two months due to excuses other than the ones specified in the regulations (e.g., accident,
death, temporary leave of the parent from the university, or difficulty adapting to the kinderg arten at the start of
the year),
5- If the family persistently behaves in a way that disrupts the school’s operation, or it becomes clear that the child
cannot adapt to the kindergarten,

6- If the child reaches the age of six and is eligible to start primary school,
7- If the family requests the child’s withdrawal for any reason.
ARTICLE 9. GTU PRESCHOOL EDUCATION CENTER’S REVENUES:
1- The fees collected from the parents of the children attending
2- Donations made to the center
ARTICLE 10. EXPENDITURES AND SPENDING OF THE GTU PRESCHOOL EDUCATION CENTER:
1- Expenses:
a) The purchase of all kinds of books, magazines, stationery, toys, videotapes, VCDs, DVDs, and other educational
materials needed to fulfill the educational purposes of the center
b) Payments for meals provided for the children through the institution's dining hall and the purchase of necessary
materials for breakfast and afternoon snacks
c) Payment s for overtime work of staff members who work through their lunch break due to the operatio nal
conditions of the preschool
d) Any expenditures required to carry out social activities that are part of the educational process
e) All expenditures required to ensure that education and care continue without interruption, as determined by the
Executive Committee
2- Expenditures: The necessary purchases are determined by the Preschool Education Center’s administration and
are carried out by the Directorate of Health, Culture and Sports.
ARTICLE 11. IMPLEMENTATION RULES:
1- The education at the Preschool Education Center is full-time; part-time education is not offered.
2- Parents are responsible for bringing their children to school and picking them up.
3- Children must not be brought to school late in a way that disrupts the educational routine.
4- Parents are not allowed to visit their children or bring guest children to the preschool, unless explicitly approved
by the Principal.
5- Parents cannot interfere with the duties of the school personnel.
6- In case of conflicts among children, parents are prohibited from intervening in matters concerning children other
than their own and must report any issues to the Principal
7- If parents wish to discuss matters related to their child or school administration, these discussions must take
place with the administration.
8- If for any reason a child cannot be brought to school, the school must be informed.
9- If a child takes home something that does not belong to them, it must be returned to the school.
ARTICLE 12. DOCUMENTS REQUIRED FOR ENROLLMENT:
1- Application form
2- A document proving that at least one parent works at GTU
3- The child's medical report from a health board
4- A copy of the child’s ID card
5- Six passport-sized photos of the child
6- Two passport-sized photos of each parent
7- Any other documents deemed necessary by the administration
ARTICLE 13. The "GTU Preschool Education Center Directive" , accepted at the GTU Senate’s meeting dated
08/09/1999 and session numbered 1999/18, is hereby repealed.
